header.delta_belief: On NovPhy's development N1 membership, three small (~1.8M-parameter) frozen world-model rankers put a 13-candidate launch sweep in order at or below chance (AUC 0.4367 cell-unit, 0.4180 member-clustered, which covers 0.5), even though 7 of 14 members are solvable at first shot. The general lesson the paper draws from this ('prediction quality is not decision quality') is already established: objective mismatch (Lambert et al. 2020) and World-in-World (cited in the paper).
header.most_damaging_issue: I3 [BLOCKER/CRITICAL, Axis 2]. The headline 'disjoint supports / success band 2–6' statistic was specified after the outcomes were seen, yet it is presented under a 'pre-registered protocol' banner. The only held-out split contradicts the band, and the statistic that does replicate on that split (cross-split AUC 0.2039 / 0.2732) is never printed.

findings.location: intro:94; synthesis:95–98 (Table 2) and :103; related_work:23; abstract:26; intro:88 (contribution 3); appendix:411
findings.quote: "Benchmark papers report agent success rates without an oracle-conditioned denominator" (intro:94); Table 2 'Per-candidate outcome & not recorded'; appendix:411 'neither reports an exhaustive per-state action ceiling over a fixed engine candidate inventory'
findings.problem: PHYRE, which the paper cites as bakhtin2019phyre, is a direct counterexample. Its tiers contain only tasks 'solvable by at least one action from this action set', solvability is certified by a binomial test over sampled actions, and it releases 'the simulation results of these 100,000 actions per task', the same actions for every task (arXiv:1908.05656, lines found via pdftotext: 'by at least one action from this action set'; 'we will release the simulation results of these 100,000 actions per task'; https://colab.research.google.com/github/facebookresearch/phyre/blob/master/examples/02_memoized_agent.ipynb). That is an oracle-conditioned denominator with per-candidate outcomes over a fixed action set. The paper's main significance claim is therefore false as written about published practice.
findings.fix: Reposition the claim. PHYRE certifies task solvability by construction; NovPhy and closed-loop world-model evaluations such as World-in-World do not. The paper's actual addition is a measured per-state ceiling over a frozen 13-candidate inventory, paired with ranker-level engine-truth AUC. Rewrite Table 2's left column as 'closed-loop world-model success rates (e.g. World-in-World)' rather than 'benchmark practice', cite PHYRE's solvability and 100k cache as the precedent, and delete the appendix:411 sentence.

findings.location: method.tex:51; synthesis:78; abstract:20; intro:78; Table 1 row 'Ordinal supports' (synthesis:60)
findings.quote: "Every result in this paper was produced under one pre-registered protocol, which fixes before any model outcome exists which units are scored" (method:51); "The structural statistics carry the result." (synthesis:78)
findings.problem: The success band [2, 6], the disjoint-supports test and the member-unit correction were specified after #87/#89 outcomes were known. The pattern '207/207 model cells chose 7–12, successes 2–6' is stated in the issue #91 comment of 2026-09-22T13:38:35Z, and the #92 selection-validity plan was frozen at 2026-09-22T14:54:42Z (selection-validity findings.md:3). This is discover-then-confirm with no holdout, presented under a pre-registration banner and never disclosed as post-outcome. The one held-out split (type010101) contradicts the band: successes appear at 0, 1 and 10–12, chosen ordinals span 0–12, and there are 42 hits. The paper handles this by narrowing the scope to N1, which is a textbook post-hoc retreat. The statistic that does replicate out of split, below-chance AUC, is never printed: zero-shot 0.2039 [0.0762, 0.3324] and few-shot 0.2732 [0.2182, 0.3239] (cross-pool summary.json cross_split.per_condition.*.auc.cell_unit).
findings.fix: (a) State in §4 and §6 that the #92 restatement (member unit, success band, disjoint supports, AUC) was specified after the #87/#89 outcomes were seen. (b) Make AUC the headline statistic, since it can be defined before any outcome is seen, and print the cross-split AUCs per condition as the held-out replication. (c) Demote 'disjoint supports' to a descriptive observation specific to N1. No new experiment is needed.

findings.quote: "Predicted-cost variance is 0.360 between states and 0.004 between actions within a state … The frozen predictors therefore learn state difficulty" (synthesis:80); "not at state solvability or state-difficulty estimation" (synthesis:83)
findings.problem: Four problems. (i) The decomposition's residual of 0.636 (summary.json ordering_mechanism.variance_decomposition.residual = 0.63607) is omitted, so the variance shares shown to the reader sum to 0.364. (ii) 'between actions within a state' mislabels an action main effect as within-state variation. (iii) The pooled Spearman 0.8776 hides the per-system values 0.4924 / 0.6130 / 0.9986 (drag_x): the sweep-ordering mechanism is essentially one system (hybrid-fixed-h1), while the two continuous rankers sit at 0.49 and 0.61. (iv) 'learn state difficulty' and 'not at state-difficulty estimation' are never tested against engine truth. No analysis relates predicted state-level cost to the ceiling indicator, and the artifact itself says 'state-blindness is NOT claimed' (selection-validity findings.md:47). A variance share shows that predictions vary across states, not that they track difficulty.
findings.fix: Print the full decomposition including the residual and the per-system ρ. Rename the 0.004 term 'action main effect'. Either drop 'or state-difficulty estimation' and 'learn state difficulty', or add the zero-engine analysis that would support them: an AUC of state-mean predicted cost against the engine-truth ceiling indicator over the 23 measurable states / 14 members, member-clustered. That analysis decides whether the positive half of the mechanism sentence stays.

findings.location: intro:46 (Fig 1 caption and panel a); §3 method:41; synthesis:78
findings.quote: "(a) Top: on the measured N1 ceiling members, engine-truth successes lie at ordinals 2–6"
findings.problem: Every ceiling state has exactly one successful ordinal. The chance terms carry k = 1 for all 7 members (summary.json chance_references.member_terms), and lookahead findings.md:25 says 'each sealed ceiling state has one successful ordinal among 9–13'. At member level the successes are {2:1, 3:1, 4:3, 5:1, 6:1}. The paper never says this, and Fig 1(a) renders 2–6 as a solid full-height band on a 'cells' axis shared with 207 chosen cells. 'Disjoint supports' therefore reduces to 'seven needles fall below the models' preferred region', which a constant a04 already hits on 5/12 states.
findings.fix: State 'exactly one successful candidate per ceiling state' in §3 and §6. In Fig 1(a), plot per-ordinal success counts in member units, not a band. Promote the per-member map (Fig 5, appendix:492) into the body, or merge it into Fig 1.

findings.location: abstract:23; intro:74; synthesis:64 (Table 1 'Lookahead'); discussion:43; row C19
findings.quote: "The failure survives 16 decision-only lookahead arms (15 at 0/36, one at 2/36, all below a 0.5 margin)"
findings.problem: Four problems. (i) The 0.5 margin is 6.4 times the top-1 chance of 0.0780, and a single arm scoring 0/36 has p ≈ (12/13)^36 = 0.056 under uniform choice (lookahead findings.md:25). An arm scoring 4× chance would still have 'survived', so the control as stated could not lose. (ii) The e600 and h1 arms roll into the regime the paper itself reports as numerically unstable ('carrier MSE reaches unstable magnitudes from t ≥ 150 at h=1', experiments:48), so their failure says nothing about whether lookahead helps. The only arm with hits, h15-e225, is a stable-carrier arm. (iii) This is a dose ladder, but its dose-response is hidden: the endpoint arms flip to the opposite end of the sweep (continuous-adaptive-e600 {0:36}, hybrid-fixed-h1-e225 {0:36}) and make 17 in-band choices in total, still with 0 hits. The 'high-arc lob' mechanism is specific to the short horizon. (iv) e225 reaches outcome resolution on only 8 of 13 successful slots (findings.md:12).
findings.fix: Report each arm against inventory-matched chance, not the 0.5 margin. Add per-arm chosen-ordinal histograms, endpoint coverage and endpoint carrier error, all from existing artifacts. Rewrite the claim as 'no arm exceeds chance; longer lookahead shifts choices toward flat shots without finding the single successful one'.

findings.quote: "the lesson is to verify the outcome channel and to test within-state candidate ordering, rather than to treat aggregate prediction quality as evidence of good decisions"
findings.problem: This cash-out is the established objective-mismatch result: 'the likelihood of one-step ahead predictions is not always correlated with control performance' (Lambert, Amos, Yadan, Calandra, L4DC 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.04523). It has also been studied in PHYRE forward-model ranking (Girdhar et al. 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10734), and World-in-World, which the paper cites, already reports that visual quality alone does not guarantee task success. None of the objective-mismatch or decision-aware model-learning line is cited (grep for lambert|mismatch|girdhar|farahmand returns 0). Related Work still covers only the retired granularity thesis plus two evaluation benchmarks.
findings.fix: Replace the granularity paragraph (related_work:21) with an objective-mismatch / decision-aware model-learning paragraph. State the portable claim as what is new: an engine-truth per-candidate AUC under a certified per-state ceiling, in a single-shot cascade regime.

findings.location: abstract:16; §3 method:37–41 (no model description); appendix A ('∼1.8M-parameter frozen-carrier predictor')
findings.quote: "We study action-conditioned world models that rank candidate actions in NovPhy"
findings.problem: The body never says what the three rankers are: architecture, input, training data, or scale. The only scale statement is in appendix A: about 1.8M parameters and 9,000 updates. The abstract generalizes to 'action-conditioned world models'. A reviewer will read the result as 'three tiny models fail on a small task', which is exactly the reading the round-2 framing verdict warned about.
findings.fix: Add a 4–5 sentence model paragraph to §3 (scale, inputs, training corpus, horizons). Scope the abstract to 'three small (~1.8M-parameter) frozen rankers'. Demanded experiment: rank the same 12 ceiling states × 13 candidates decision-only with one pretrained world model (e.g. DINO-WM, already in the bib) against the existing verdict table. This needs zero engine seconds and would change the verdict because it separates 'these models fail' from 'action-conditioned ranking fails in this regime'.

axis_passes.axis1: The 10-minute test surfaces the N1 failure, so a Δbelief exists but is narrow. Anchor: MAJOR, the portable lesson is prior art (I7). Fig 1 carries the tension visually, judged on the rendered page-2 asset; the band shading is flagged (I5). The 'A+B+C combo' item is n/a.
axis_passes.axis2: Falsifiability: the headline is post-hoc and the lookahead margin could not lose (I3, I6). HARKing scan: 10 bare-fact occurrences in the body files. The three most damaging are synthesis:80 'The frozen predictors therefore learn state difficulty…', synthesis:78 'The structural statistics carry the result.', and discussion:39 'Registry row C16 is therefore answered: the zero is a ranking failure on solvable states'. Wording register: pass (no prove/confirm). Statistical hygiene: I12. Refutation check: the type010101 split refuted the band and was answered by narrowing scope, which corroborates I3.

axis_passes.findings_checklist: (1) Phenomenon framed as a conflict between community beliefs: weak, because the 'assumed denominator' premise is false for PHYRE (I2). (2) Primary analysis designated: partial — Table 1 is declared primary, but AUC, disjoint supports and top-k are treated as co-equal. (3) Each cross-check kills a named alternative: pass (exposure → memorization; determinism → noise; constants → 'use a fixed angle'), with the lookahead check weak (I6). (4) Dose ladder: present but its dose-response (the chosen-ordinal shift) is unreported (I6). (5) Cash-out: present, but it is prior art (I7).

coherence_review: The abstract → intro → §6 → discussion → conclusion chain tells one consistent ranking-failure story, and the numbers agree across all of them. The dead thesis still occupies §3/§3.1/§4/§5 and contributions 1–2 (I10). The +0.0887 contrast still reads as supported through 'family-conditional in sign' (I9). All \ref targets resolve (0 '??'), but every 'row C10–C21' pointer dangles in the rendered PDF (I1). Section-title check: §4 'Pre-Registered Matched-System Protocol' is contradicted by the post-hoc #92 restatement (I3), and 'matched-system' belongs to the retired thesis.
score_vs_baseline: The round-2 predicted hybrid was 6/10. The implemented text fixes every round-1 and round-2 wording alarm: dichotomy removed, quantifier scoped, reversal framed first-person, adaptive-controller limitation disclosed, per-seed values printed. Against a fresh reader it still scores 4/10, for five reasons: the registry does not render (I1), the denominator novelty claim is false for PHYRE (I2), the headline statistic is post-hoc and failed its own holdout (I3), the mechanism evidence is overstated (I4, I6), and the portable lesson is objective mismatch (I7). Fixing I1–I7 and I10–I11 in writing, with no new experiments beyond the zero-engine state-level AUC in I4, would plausibly restore 5–6. The pretrained-ranker experiment in I8 is what could reach 6+.
top3_rejection_risks: 1. Post-hoc headline with a failed holdout (I3): method:51, synthesis:78, abstract:20. The band / disjoint-supports story was specified after the outcomes were seen and does not replicate on type010101; the replicating AUC is unprinted.

2. Significance and novelty (I2 + I7): intro:94, synthesis:95–103, abstract:26. PHYRE already certifies solvability and releases per-action outcomes, and 'prediction quality ≠ decision quality' is the objective-mismatch result. Compounded by narrowness: three ~1.8M-parameter rankers and 7 clusters, with model scale undisclosed in the body (I8).

3. Mechanism overclaim and weak controls (I4 + I6): intro:78, synthesis:80–83, Table 1:64. The residual 0.636 and per-system ρ 0.49/0.61/0.9986 are hidden, the state-difficulty claim is untested, and the lookahead check runs against a 0.5 margin with unstable-carrier arms. The mechanical but desk-visible I1 (registry rows C10–C21 invisible) must be fixed first.
